entities.summary: Quintus Remmius Palaemon Quintus Rhemnius Fannius Palaemon was a Roman grammarian and native of Vicentia living during the reigns of Emperors Tiberius and Claudius. He was a prominent figure in the Roman literary circle, and his works on Latin grammar and rhetoric were widely studied. Palaemon's most notable achievement was the compilation of a comprehensive Latin dictionary, which became a standard reference for scholars for centuries. His grammatical treatises influenced the development of Latin language and literature, shaping the way Latin was taught and written. Palaemon's legacy extends beyond his written works, as his emphasis on the importance of Latin language and culture contributed to the Roman Empire's cultural dominance. The Roman poet Martial credited Palaemon with inspiring his own writing style, stating 'Palaemon's grammar is my grammar'. Palaemon's life and work demonstrate the enduring impact of Roman culture on Western civilization. The Roman historian Suetonius noted Palaemon's involvement in the imperial court, highlighting the importance of literary patronage during the reigns of Tiberius and Claudius.
